clue.text: Passion dominates game, we hear, in pointless tennis position

indicators.note: the game's sound-alike is placed in the middle of the tennis score

parts.note: love all is the score in tennis when neither player has a point

indicators.note: signals that the game's name is only heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: conkers is a British children's game of swinging horse chestnuts on strings

explanation.surface: A tennis commentary in which emotion takes over a game still level at no points each.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British schoolyard game played with horse chestnuts on strings; love all is the tennis score when neither side has won a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says affection overcomes every obstacle, so passion prevailing over everything is its meaning.

clue.text: Spy Indian princess rejecting article without thanks

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside: the shortened princess surrounds the word for thanks
the princess throws out the article, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a maharani is the wife of a maharaja or a princess in her own right
an is the indefinite article
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: An Indian royal turns spy, refusing an item and giving no thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and ta is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mata Hari was the Dutch dancer executed in 1917 as a German secret agent, now the byword for a female spy.

clue.text: One showing Mary pastry case from trattoria

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: the word whose outside letters are used

explanation.surface: Someone at an Italian restaurant shows Mary a pastry case.
explanation.walkthrough: The case of 'trattoria' is its outer letters, T and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin holding the dead Christ, so it depicts Mary.

clue.text: Opener gets run out in captivating draw

parts.note: a start is an opening

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, so these are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cricket opening batsman is run out in a match that ends drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words mislead: 'run out' is the letters of RUN shuffled to URN, and 'draw' is an attraction rather than a tied match.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main act of a show, the performer who pulls in the crowds.

clue.text: Many runs perhaps in Twenty20?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: runs are ... in cricket, and Twenty20 is literally twenty and twenty, two ...

explanation.walkthrough: Twenty20 is a short form of cricket; a score is also twenty, so the name itself is two scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Scores means a great number of things, and in cricket the runs a batsman makes are what is scored.

clue.text: Shrewder retaining ball, male player

indicators.note: the word for shrewder holds the other letters within it

parts.note: wiser means shrewder
O is shaped like a ball
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A sharper sportsman keeps hold of the ball, as a male player should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' is not a sportsman here but someone who plays the field romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is slang for a man who pursues many romantic partners, which is what a womaniser does.

clue.text: Thoroughly soppy git by place of retreat

parts.note: sod and git are both British insults for an unpleasant person
a den is a private room to retreat to

explanation.surface: A sentimental fool is found next to his hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Soppy usually means sentimental, but here it is read literally as soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy can mean saturated with water, and sodden means soaked through.

clue.text: Blunt answer's received about legislative measure

indicators.note: the two words together take in the short word for about

parts.note: a blunt is cannabis rolled in a cigar wrapper, so a joint
a solution is an answer
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A curt reply is met with a legislative proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' looks like an adjective describing the answer, but it is drug slang for cannabis rolled in a cigar leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US Congress a joint resolution is a measure passed by both houses that has the force of law.

clue.text: Performing twice in Tosca is stimulating for a soloist?

indicators.note: performing means putting on an act, so these letters act out a new order

parts.note: twice asks for the neighbouring word in a second time, so its letters appear again
taken as written
the opera's name, used as letters

explanation.surface: Someone appears twice in a Puccini opera, which inspires a solo singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The soloist is not a singer: the definition is a sly description of self-pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Onanistic means relating to masturbation, a solo form of sexual stimulation.

clue.text: Refurbished loo contains very old moulding

indicators.note: the shuffled loo holds the two abbreviations
refurbished means done up anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A renovated toilet has a very old decorative trim.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex architectural moulding with a quarter-circle profile.

clue.text: Demanding person from Oldham needing a break?

indicators.note: the town's name must be broken in two, so it is read as two separate words rather than one place

parts.note: broken into old ham: old is EX, as in former, and a ham is an overacting performer, so ACTOR

explanation.surface: Someone from the Lancashire town of Oldham is out of work and wants a lucky chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Oldham is a town near Manchester; 'needing a break' tells you to split it into OLD HAM, and a resting actor does need a break.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts, insisting firmly on payment or obedience from others.

clue.text: African fish's name maybe grasped by sailors

indicators.note: the sailors hold the name between them

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
in the film A Fish Called Wanda, the fish is named Wanda

explanation.surface: Sailors grab an African fish that may have a name.
explanation.walkthrough: The film A Fish Called Wanda gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rwandan is a person from Rwanda in East Africa.

clue.text: Conservative going kind of pink, concerned with speech

indicators.note: the Conservative goes away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: coral is a pinkish shade

explanation.surface: A Tory politician turning pinkish while giving a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral describes what is spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Person grilling odd sandwiches is not out to lunch

indicators.note: the word for odd encloses the other letters like bread round a filling

parts.note: queer means odd or strange

indicators.note: an idiom for crazy, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strange figure eating sandwiches says he is not away at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out to lunch' looks like part of the picture of a lunch break, but it is an idiom for crazy and so signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A questioner is an interrogator, and grilling is slang for intense questioning.

clue.text: Take in various keys, say, and polish roughly

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so the letters are only loosely in place and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Visiting many tropical keys and buffing something casually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keys, say' are not for locks but low islands like the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: To island-hop is to travel from one small island to another, visiting several in turn.

clue.text: What reprobates do after some tobacco's in pocket

indicators.note: the reprobates' act comes after the tobacco

parts.note: a quid is a lump of chewing tobacco
reprobates sin

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers keep some chewing tobacco in their pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is also British slang for a pound, which helps the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quids in is a British phrase for being in profit, having come out ahead financially.

clue.text: Boxing a long time, clobber despicable people

indicators.note: the clothes box in the stretch of time, holding it inside

parts.note: clobber and togs are both British slang for clothes
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: A boxer takes a long time to beat up some contemptible people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' and 'clobber' look like fighting words, but clobber is slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is British slang for a worthless or contemptible person.

clue.text: Gaudy little skirts are popular with consumers

indicators.note: to skirt is to go round, so the small word surrounds the other

parts.note: tiny means little
products that sell are popular with buyers

explanation.surface: Short skirts are a hit with shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinselly means showy and cheaply glittering, like tinsel decoration.

clue.text: One nameless dreamer with a bouquet

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: without the abbreviation for name, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a romantic is an idealistic dreamer

explanation.surface: An anonymous dreamer clutching a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name; 'bouquet' is a scent, not flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic means fragrant, and a wine's bouquet is its pleasant smell.

clue.text: Establishing distance from two directions before time rambling

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south
ranging means roaming or rambling

explanation.surface: Someone drifts apart after going two ways and wandering about for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranging means alienating, putting emotional distance between people.

clue.text: Revolutionary Communist wears brown, without exception

indicators.note: the Communist is inside the brown as if dressed in it

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Mao Zedong was the Chinese Communist leader

explanation.surface: A revolutionary Communist dresses in brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' sounds like a description of Mao but is the signal to turn MAO into OAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To a man is an idiom meaning every single one, all without exception.

clue.text: Banking centre, say, raised what's held in Russian banks

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for for example, say
the Neva is the river flowing through St Petersburg, held between its banks

explanation.surface: A finance centre where cash is kept in Russian banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian banks are riverbanks, enclosing the Neva.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva in Switzerland is a major centre for private banking and finance.

clue.text: Cash returns for Jack, say

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for cash is read backwards

parts.note: loot is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A man called Jack hands back some money.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is not a man but the lifting device for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a tool for raising a heavy object such as a car.

clue.text: Son has ice cream or small cake

parts.note: a cone is an ice cream in a wafer cornet

explanation.surface: A boy chooses between an ice cream and a little cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small, plain baked cake usually served with butter or jam.

clue.text: Invest and invest, investing reserve

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe, so the answer is clothed in these words

explanation.surface: Repeated advice to put money in, by putting money into savings.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of the first word, all of 'and', and the start of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute, like a reserve player who replaces another.

clue.text: Liking less parking in transport

indicators.note: less means minus, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a penchant is a liking

explanation.surface: Someone who is no fan of parking in public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' is the verb meaning to enrapture, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport someone is to carry them away with delight, as to enchant does.

clue.text: Plain Welsh seaside resort, no northern dud

indicators.note: no means without, so the letters are removed

parts.note: Llandudno is a seaside resort in north Wales
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A dull Welsh coastal town with nothing worth seeing up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the resort but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a vast grassy plain in South America, especially in Venezuela.

clue.text: Screen star in a period of abstention cutting alcohol

indicators.note: the period cuts into the drink, sitting inside it

parts.note: vino is informal for wine
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A film star, mid-Lent, cuts down on drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Lent is the forty days before Easter when Christians traditionally give something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was the silent-film heartthrob of the 1920s.
